segments.text: Every video says Earth tips over without the Moon. It doesn't.

In 1993, a famous study found that without the Moon, Earth's tilt could swing anywhere from zero all the way to eighty-five degrees. At eighty-five degrees, Earth would be lying on its side, with months of endless day and months of endless night.
But in 2012, NASA scientist Jack Lissauer and his team ran much more detailed simulations. Their answer was far calmer.
Earth would wobble more than it does today, but in their simulations it stayed roughly between twelve and thirty-eight degrees, even over a hundred million years.
But no sudden flip. And no instant freeze.
Not tonight. And not because of the tilt.
